This Functional Specification Document defines how Pulse AI is expected to behave from a functional perspective. It translates the current Emerson requirements and Pulse AI product plan into modules, actors, states, business rules, data interactions, interfaces, validations, errors and acceptance criteria. Items dependent on unconfirmed business policy are explicitly marked Proposed or TBD.
Web client: role-based employee, manager, HR, Finance and Director experiences.
Application/API layer: authentication context, authorization, workflow logic, validation, reporting and audit operations.
SQL data store: employee, user/role, timesheet, status, salary/finance metadata, notification and audit records.
AI service: anomaly/validation support, summaries and permission-aware assistant capabilities.
Notification/background processing: missing-submission checks, reminders and workflow event delivery.
External enterprise systems: identity, HR/ERP, payroll/invoice, attendance and communication services where later confirmed.
Create/update own eligible draft timesheet; submit; view own history/status; correct rejected records; receive notifications; permitted assistant queries.
View assigned employee submissions; approve/reject eligible timesheets; monitor missing submissions; review anomaly evidence; permitted assistant/reporting.
Maintain/import employee master data; view HR-scoped employee/timesheet compliance; audit HR operations.
View approved eligible hours; prepare/export payroll-ready data and invoice drafts; view finance audit/traceability.
View authorized organization-level analytics and reports; drill down only where permission permits.
Evaluate missing submissions, create notifications, run configured anomaly checks and maintain processing status.
Draft → Submitted → Approved OR Rejected → Resubmitted → Approved

System resolves user role and permitted organizational scope.

System loads the employee's period and existing entries.

Entry stored as eligible draft when valid.

System performs final validation and prevents submission when blocking rules fail.
Employee can view rejection reason, correct eligible entries and resubmit.
System returns own authorized timesheet periods and status.
Reject or flag non-numeric, negative or missing required values.
System applies Emerson-configured daily/weekly thresholds when finalized.
Blocking error or warning per policy.
Detection service creates an explainable finding linked to affected entries.
System stores finding type, evidence/explanation, severity/confidence if supported, and review state.
Anomaly does not automatically approve/reject the timesheet.
System returns submitted timesheets within manager's assigned scope.
System shows entries, totals, deterministic validation and AI anomaly evidence.
System records approval actor/time and transitions status according to configured workflow.
System requires rejection reason and records actor/time/reason.
System provides revision comparison where previous version exists.
System includes only records eligible under the configured policy and excludes blocked/anomalous cases as defined.
System identifies employees without required submitted timesheets.
System creates an alert/reminder for the appropriate employee/user.
Channel, schedule, escalation and retry behavior follow finalized Emerson policy.
System accepts the approved input format and validates records.
System prevents or flags invalid/duplicate data according to configured identity rules.
System supports upload, column mapping, validation preview and commit.
System distinguishes created, updated, skipped and failed rows and provides error details.
System returns employee information within HR scope; restricted compensation remains permission-controlled.
System returns approved work-hour data within authorized scope.
System aggregates eligible approved time and exposes exceptions before generation.
System formats approved work-hour data into the finalized payroll-ready structure.
System uses eligible approved/billable work-hour data to assist preparation of client invoices.
System exposes traceability from export/invoice line to source approved timesheet entries.
System returns fields only when role/scope grants access.
System returns role-appropriate submission, approval and workforce indicators.
System prioritizes organization-level aggregates, period comparisons and material exceptions.
System limits results to authorized scope regardless of UI filter input.
Equivalent readable summary/table is available for accessibility.
System determines actor role/scope before retrieving data for the assistant.
Only authorized data is provided to the AI/tooling layer.
Assistant refuses or limits the response without exposing protected data.
Result includes understandable source/report links where available and clearly indicates read-only behavior.
Assistant uses approved application/reporting tools rather than arbitrary SQL.
Model/API, data minimization, retention, logging and enterprise privacy policy must be confirmed before production.
System records actor, timestamp, action, target record, previous/new state where relevant and scope.
System returns audit events only within that user's permitted scope.
Audit record links generated output to source data and generating actor/process.
A user may access only records and fields permitted by role and organizational scope.
A timesheet belongs to a specific employee and period and must be associated with the submitting employee.
Invalid numeric values, negative hours and missing required fields must not pass final submission validation.
Maximum/expected daily and weekly hours, overtime and leave handling are configurable only after stakeholder confirmation.
AI/anomaly output is advisory; approval authority remains with authorized users.
A rejection requires a reason and creates a visible correction/resubmission path.
Only approved work-hour data is eligible for downstream payroll/invoice preparation.
Generated finance outputs retain traceability to source approved time.
Salary/compensation information is restricted and is not exposed merely because a user can view timesheets.
Notification timing, recipients, channel and escalation depend on Emerson policy.
Multi-level approval sequence, delegation and escalation depend on Emerson policy.
Approved periods are locked from ordinary employee editing unless an authorized reopen/correction process is defined.

All protected APIs must derive/validate authenticated actor context server-side.
Client-supplied role or employee identifiers must not be trusted as authorization evidence.
Timesheet APIs should support read current period, save/update eligible draft, submit, history/detail and correction/resubmission where policy permits.
Manager APIs should support scoped queue/list, review detail, approve/reject and missing-submission reporting.
HR APIs should support employee list/detail and controlled import validation/commit.
Finance APIs should support approved-hour retrieval, export preview/generation/history and invoice preparation/traceability once rules are finalized.
AI endpoints should expose only approved, permission-filtered application/reporting operations.
External integrations must use explicit contracts for authentication, fields, errors, retries and audit logging.
Return permission-denied state without leaking record existence or restricted fields.
Keep user context, identify affected field/entry and explain corrective action.
Do not transition to Submitted; show consolidated blocking issues.
Do not fabricate findings; surface degraded status and preserve deterministic validation/workflow where safe.
Do not silently commit invalid row; show field/value/reason and permit correction.
Prevent generation for affected records and identify the exception.
Record failure/retry state according to finalized integration policy.
Prevent silent overwrite; require refresh/retry or use version-aware update semantics.
Enforce authorization at the API/data layer, not only in the user interface.
Restrict salary/compensation and billing-sensitive data to explicitly authorized users.
Log material privileged actions and finance output generation.
Minimize data sent to external AI services and apply the approved enterprise AI/privacy policy.
Prevent the assistant from bypassing application permissions or executing unrestricted database queries.
Validate uploaded HR data and treat file/import content as untrusted input.
Employee can create a valid draft, see deterministic issues, review and submit; blocking errors prevent submission; resulting status is visible.
Manager sees only assigned scope, can inspect evidence, approve eligible submissions or reject with a reason; decision is traceable.
Employee can identify rejection reason, correct eligible data and resubmit; manager can distinguish the revision.
System can identify outstanding required submissions and surface actionable notifications/views.
HR can validate before commit; invalid/duplicate records are identified; results distinguish successful and failed rows.
Only approved eligible time is included; exceptions are visible; generated output can be traced to source records.
Organization-level metrics are available within authorized scope without default exposure of individual restricted compensation.
Assistant answers supported authorized questions, refuses unauthorized requests and never exposes data beyond actor permissions.
12. Open Decisions Required Before Final FSD
Approved UI mockup and final screen/field/action mapping.
Timesheet cadence, period boundaries, project/task fields, expected hours, overtime and leave rules.
Edit/lock/reopen policy after submission and approval.
Manager assignment, approval levels, delegation, escalation and bulk approval rules.
HR import schema/file type and create/update matching rules.
Payroll-ready export schema and whether Pulse AI stores salary, calculates salary, or only prepares work-hour inputs.
Billing rates, invoice fields, client/project relationships and invoice lifecycle.
Notification channels, timing, escalation, retries and user preferences.
Authentication/SSO mechanism and enterprise identity integration.
AI model/provider, anomaly approach, approved assistant tools, data retention/privacy and external-LLM policy.

This FSD is a functional baseline, not a declaration that all listed Proposed behaviors are approved Emerson business rules. Final implementation should promote Proposed/TBD items to Confirmed only after mockup review and stakeholder validation.
